source_text: Ac per hoc negare quemquam pro alterius peccato posse damnari, negare ullum peccatum ad posteros naturae condicione transire atque credere atque asserere hominem de instituta a Deo fecunditate genitum liberi arbitrii iustis legibus conveniri, ut vitet omne, quod malum est, exerceat omne, quod bonum est, nec secundum vos aestimet amorem et necessitatem criminum substantiae suae causis, id est ipsis adhaesisse seminibus nec recipiat tam stultam, tam insanam, tam impiam sententiam in contumeliam videlicet naturae rationis Dei Apostoli volumine contineri, quia dixerit per unum hominem peccatum in hunc mundum intrasse et in omnes homines transisse mortem [n194] , cum hoc diu caligare non siverit, addens eos, quos omnes dixerat, debere multos intellegi, qui imitatione, non generatione peccassent [n195] .
pass_a_gloss: And through this to deny that anyone can be damned for another's sin, to deny that any sin passes to posterity by a condition of nature, and to believe and assert that a human being begotten from a fecundity instituted by God is convened by just laws of free decision, so that he avoid everything that is evil, exercise everything that is good, and not according to you estimate that a love and necessity of crimes have clung to the causes of his substance, that is to the seeds themselves, and not receive so foolish, so insane, so impious a sentence as contained in the volume of the Apostle unto an insult namely of nature, of reason, of God, because he said that through one human being sin entered into this world and death passed into all human beings, when he did not long allow this to be dark, adding that those whom he had said all ought to be understood as many, who had sinned by imitation, not by generation.

pass_b_english: Consequently, they teach us to deny that anyone can be condemned for another’s sin, and to deny that any sin passes to descendants as a condition of nature. They teach us to believe and assert that a human being born through the fertility God instituted is addressed by the just laws of free will: to avoid everything evil and practice everything good. Such a person should not suppose, as you do, that a love and necessity of crimes clings to the causes of his substance—to the seed itself. Nor should he accept that so foolish, insane, and impious a statement, insulting nature, reason, and God, is contained in the apostle’s book merely because he said sin entered this world through one man and death passed into all human beings (Romans 5:12). For he did not allow this to remain obscure for long, but added that those he had called ‘all’ should be understood as ‘many,’ who sinned through imitation, not generation (Romans 5:19).

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
